The Zamucoan languages, including Ayoreo and Chamacoco, exhibit a fusional typological profile with a dominant SVO basic word order in declarative clauses, though flexibility arises for pragmatic purposes such as focalization or emphasis. It is also known as Xamicoco or Xamacoco, although the tribe itself prefers the name Ishír (which is also spelled Ɨshɨr, Ishiro, Yshyr) and sometimes Jewyo. What are the four dialects of Chamacoco? Four dialects of Chamacoco have been identified: Héiwo, in the Fuerte Olimpo area; Ebidóso and Hório, spoken in the Bahía Negra region; and Tomaráho, in the Alto Paraná Atlantic forests. The speakers of Hório and Ebidóso were estimated to be 800 in 1970. Fewer than 200 people spoke Tomaráho then.
